title: A tool much larger than the feature it is assigned to is accepted at edit time (e.g. a 100 mm end mill on a 6 mm pocket)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens: `edit_operation` / `set_tool` accept a cutter that cannot fit the feature at all - in the local-model benchmark (2026-11-22, CamCraft v0.25.0 over MCP), "use a 100 mm end mill in the 6 mm pocket" was applied by every large model (ornith-1.5 35B, qwen3.8, qwen3-coder, qwen3.6) and the edit succeeded. Generation later refuses it, but by then the operation is changed and the user (or the AI chat) gets no early, named reason.

Expected: assigning a tool whose cutting diameter exceeds the feature's smallest width (pocket/slot width, hole diameter for bore/thread mill) is refused at the command - or accepted with a named warning - stating both sizes ("tool Ø100 mm is wider than the 6 mm pocket"). Same rule for a person in the UI and for MCP/AI callers (one command path).

Evidence: benchmark task `t3_absurd_tool`, results in the benchmark report (summary.md on M5, ~/bench/local-models/results/); small models declined, large models applied it.

Done means: a pinning test - assigning a tool wider than the operation's feature returns a named refusal (or warning) at command time naming both sizes, for 2D Pocket and Slot at least; the UI shows the same message; existing valid assignments are unchanged.
